text: In LiteRT-LM agello-next (7b872544) and the v0.18.0 source, with the executor's own sampler (SessionConfig::UseExternalSampler false, the default; no non-test code sets it), LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase::Decode keeps the last token of every decode step or MTP round as the pending input token, counted in current_step but not yet written to the KV cache; when that token is a stop token, Tasks' stop filter drops it from the text and the decode loop ends, so after a reply that ended on a stop token as the last token of its step, the stop token is the executor's pending token.

In agello-next and the v0.18.0 source, PrefillInternal writes a pending input token first, at its own position, before the prefill's tokens; so after a Gemma 4 E2B/E4B reply without reasoning that ended on '<turn|>' (106), the next user message's prefill (the render difference, which starts with '<|turn>user
' because the previous render already ends with '<turn|>
') is written right after the '<turn|>' slot, and the '
' (107) that the file template puts after '<turn|>' is never in the KV cache.

sources.detail: section 0 jinja_prompt_template: '<turn|>\n' after every non-tool message; a tool message renders '<|tool_response>...<tool_response|>' with no turn header; no generation prompt after a tool response

text: In agello-next and the v0.18.0 source, a pending token produced by decode is a TokenData holding only its id (the executor looks up embeddings only for a prefill's last token and, in GetTokenToDecode, for the token about to be decoded), and FillInputBufferWithToken writes a token without embedding as its int32 id in the first 4 bytes of the input and zeros after it; for the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B files, whose prefill signatures take embeddings and per-layer embeddings rather than token ids, the stop token that the next prefill writes first therefore gets that id-and-zeros row in both inputs instead of its embedding, so its KV entry is not computed from '<turn|>'.

sources.detail: signature prefill_1024 inputs: embeddings FLOAT32[1, 1024, 2560], per_layer_embeddings FLOAT32[1, 1024, 42, 256], no token-id input

text:
In agello-next, after SetCurrentStep moves current_step below the processed-token count (as the channel-content filter's rewind does), the next prefill's RollBackProcessedTokens truncates the processed tokens and re-adds the token at current_step - 1 as a new id-only pending TokenData; after the filter's rewind to the checkpoint saved after the user prefill, that token is the '
' ending '<|turn>model
', so the refill prefill rewrites that position from an id-and-zeros row while the rest of the refill ('...<turn|>', with the final '
' left pending with its embedding looked up) matches the template's render.

In agello-next and the v0.18.0 source, when an MTP round emits the stop token before its last emitted token, DecodeOneStep::Run moves the executor's current_step back by sequence_length - step, which drops the tokens after the stop token and the stop token itself; the next prefill then re-pends the token before the stop token (as an id-only TokenData, rewriting its position from an id-and-zeros row), so neither '<turn|>' nor the '\n' after it is in the KV cache at that turn boundary.

In both builds, after a Gemma 4 E2B/E4B tool-call reply without reasoning that stopped on '<|tool_response>' (50) or '<turn|>' (106), the stop token is pending and the tool message's prefill difference starts with '<|tool_response>' (the previous render already ends '<tool_call|><turn|>
', and the file template adds no generation prompt after a tool response); the KV cache then holds '<tool_call|>', the stop token's slot (an id-and-zeros row), then '<|tool_response>response:...<tool_response|>', where the render has '<tool_call|><turn|>
<|tool_response>'; and the answer generated after the tool response follows '<tool_response|>' directly, while later renders put '<|turn>model
' before it.

text: Conversation::GetTokenCount returns the executor's current_step, which counts the pending token (ProcessedTokens::TokenCount is the processed tokens plus one when a token is pending); compared with the token count of the Gemma 4 file template's render of the same history (assuming the model's tokens equal the render's encoding of its text), it is 1 lower for each reply without reasoning that ended with its stop token pending (a tool-call reply included), 2 lower instead when an MTP round emitted the stop token before its last token, a further 3 lower for an answer generated right after a tool response without reasoning (the '<|turn>model\n' later renders put before it), and equal after an agello-next reasoning refill.
formula: render '<turn|>\n' = 2 tokens (106, 107) vs 1 cache slot -> -1 per reply; MTP stop before the round's last token: 0 slots -> -2; answer after a tool response: '<|turn>model\n' (105, 4368, 107) absent -> -3 more; reasoning refill writes the render's tokens -> 0

text: In agello-next and the v0.18.0 source, LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic::Prefill passes the KV state's entries minus current_step to GetOptimizedPrefillWorkGroups, which charges every work group the full length of its prefill signature, padded or not, and fails with FailedPrecondition when they don't fit; so no prefill, the channel filter's refill included, writes past the allocated context, and with E4B's prefill_128 and prefill_1024 signatures every prefill fails when fewer than 128 positions remain, however few tokens it carries.

sources.detail: signatures prefill_1024 and prefill_128 (mask BOOL[1, 1, 1024, 32003] and [1, 1, 128, 32003])

text: For the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B files the executor's max_num_tokens equals the allocated context N (the context target is maxNumTokens below 32,003, else 32,000, and ClampMaxNumTokens lowers a larger maxNumTokens to the state's entries); a plain decode step writes only position current_step - 1 and Tasks::Decode stops once current_step reaches max_num_tokens, so plain decode never writes past position N - 1.

In agello-next and the v0.18.0 source, nothing on the MTP path compares the verify positions with the cache size (Tasks::Decode, LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase::Decode, EnsureMtpDrafterLoaded and LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter::Draft have no such check): a round runs at the first decode after a prefill and whenever the decode loop continues (current_step < max_num_tokens), and its verify run covers positions p..p+3 with p = current_step - 1 in a primed round and p = current_step (taken before the priming step) in a priming round; with N allocated positions (0..N-1), a primed round reaches position N + 1 at most and a priming round right after a prefill that filled the cache to N reaches N + 3.
formula: primed: loop continues only while c <= N - 1, p = c - 1, last position p + 3 = c + 2 <= N + 1; priming: a prefill leaves c <= N (X-GAP-008), the priming step writes c - 1, Draft gets position c, last position c + 3 <= N + 3

text: On the GPU in our build (LiteRT 362759838), the verify run's key and value writes at positions at or beyond the cache's size are skipped: the add_values_to_cache kernel returns when params[0] + X >= cache_size or >= params[1] (non-ring form), and cache_size is an odml.cache_update attribute that LiteRT rewrites from 32003 to the allocated context, so an MTP round near the end doesn't write past the KV buffers; positions beyond the end are not stored.

In agello-next and the v0.18.0 source, PrepareVerifierInputBuffers fills the verify signature's attention mask (BOOL[1, 1, 4, N] for E4B after the context rewrite) on the CPU with FillAttentionMask from p for 4 rows, and for a causal mask (the Gemma 4 files have no executor metadata, so causal) FillAttentionMask fills row k up to column p + k + 1 without clamping to N; when p + 3 >= N the fill runs into the next row and, for the last row, p + 4 - N bytes past the end of the 4N-byte tensor: at most 2 bytes in a primed round and at most 4 in a priming round right after a prefill that filled the cache.
formula: last row ends at element 3N + (p + 3) + 1 = 3N + p + 4; past the end by 3N + p + 4 - 4N = p + 4 - N; primed p <= N - 2 -> <= 2; priming p <= N -> <= 4

text: Where the verify-mask overrun lands depends on the mask's buffer: when no GPU consumer registers requirements for a BOOL mask, LiteRT-LM's CreateInputBuffer falls back to host memory, which LiteRT (362759838) allocates with posix_memalign of the buffer size plus XNN_EXTRA_BYTES and zero-fills that tail (XNN_EXTRA_BYTES is 16 when LiteRT is built without its CPU path, XNNPACK's own value otherwise); which buffer type the verify mask gets on Metal, and what a write past a Metal buffer's tensor size hits, were not traced.

In LiteRT-LM agello-next and v0.18.0, the C API's conversation stream callback (CreateConversationCallback in c/conversation.cc) turns every error status it receives into a chunk with is_final true and the error text, and the empty message into a final chunk without error; it keeps no state, so it passes on every terminal event the conversation layer produces.

In LiteRT-LM agello-next and v0.18.0, for a Gemma 4 conversation with tools in its preface, one tool-call block that the FC parser rejects produces two error chunks with is_final true for the same send: when the block's end fence streams, the internal callback's SendMessage passes the failed ToMessage status (InvalidArgument, because return_error_on_parse_failure defaults to true and neither the C API nor Swift changes it) to the user callback and the stream goes on; at the end of decode SendCompleteMessage parses the whole reply again, fails on the same block, and sends a second error.

Both the Swift wrapper Agello ships (85b1a776) and the one at the agello-next pin release the StreamContext retained for a send on every chunk that carries an error, whatever is_final says, as well as on the first final chunk, and sendMessageStream keeps no other reference to the context once the stream has started; a second error chunk for the same send therefore reads the context through takeUnretainedValue and releases it again after the first release freed it, a use-after-free and over-release on LiteRT-LM's thread.

The other terminal paths of the conversation layer deliver one terminal event per send: SendCompleteMessage returns after reporting an extraction or parse error without sending the end sentinel; the internal callback's error, cancelled, failed and token-limit-error branches each make one user callback and return; and in agello-next, when the channel-filter refill reports an error itself, the deferred end sentinel is suppressed.

Both Swift wrappers (85b1a776 and the pin) also finish the stream and release the StreamContext on a non-final chunk whose text isn't valid JSON or doesn't convert to a Message, while the native stream continues, so later chunks of that send reach a released context.

In LiteRT-LM agello-next and v0.18.0, LlgConstraint::ComputeNext commits the token into the llguidance constraint object of the state it is given (llg_commit_token on that state's pointer) and returns a copy of that state, which shares the same object through a shared_ptr; only Start() clones a fresh object, so every state derived from one Start() is the same mutable llguidance matcher.

In an MTP round with an llguidance constraint (agello-next and v0.18.0), RunDraftingLoop computes each draft's mask from the current state and then commits the draft with ComputeNext, so by verification the verified state and the three draft states all point to the matcher after drafts d1, d2 and d3; RunVerification computes all four row masks from those states, so verifier rows 0 to 2 get the mask for the position after d3 instead of their own position, and only row 3 is right.

After verification (agello-next and v0.18.0), LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter::Draft sets the verified state to draft state n (the same matcher, already holding d1 to d3) and commits the bonus token, so the matcher ends at verified tokens + d1 d2 d3 + bonus whatever n is; that matches the emitted tokens only when all 3 drafts are accepted; after a rejection the matcher holds rejected drafts, later masks are computed from that state, and the bonus commit can fail, making Draft return InternalError ("Failed to commit token").

The priming step is consistent (agello-next): the priming plain decode is masked by ConstrainedDecoder's own state, a separate Start() clone that DecodeLogitsImpl doesn't advance with the prompt's last token (ran_decode is false after a prefill), and Draft then resets the drafter's state to a fresh Start() and commits the priming token; ConstrainedDecoder::UpdateState is not called during MTP rounds and advances only on plain decode steps, which within a decode task with MTP on is the priming step only.

Consequence: with speculative decoding on and an llguidance constraint (a JSON schema or a regex response format), the documented build and the v0.18.0 source can emit tokens the grammar doesn't allow: a rejection's bonus token is picked under the mask of the position after d3, and a rejected draft stays committed in the matcher; this matches Agello's on-device observation (LM-SWIFT-059), so MTP must stay off for constrained conversations at the pin too, and it is a correctness bug to report upstream.

Agello (93122b6) starts a chat reply only when the window minus the tokens in use, the input estimate and a 64-token margin leaves at least 96 tokens, and caps the reply at that room; with exact counts, a send's prefill then has at least its input plus 160 positions free, more than the at most input + 127 that E4B's prefill_128 runs need, and its decode stops 64 positions before the end of the window plus at most one MTP round's tokens, so it stays clear of the positions an MTP round can reach past the end.
formula: room = maxNumTokens - used - input - 64 >= 96 -> free positions before the prefill = maxNumTokens - used >= input + 160; a 128-run plan needs ceil(L / 128) x 128 <= L + 127; decode stops at used + input + room = maxNumTokens - 64, overshot by at most 4 tokens of one round

text: Agello (93122b6) streams chat replies with Conversation.sendMessageStream on conversations that declare CurrentDateTimeTool and CalculatorTool when tools are enabled and WebSearchTool when options.webSearchTool is set, so in those chats a tool-call block that the parser rejects reaches the two-error-chunk path of the shipped wrapper.
